links.outcome: Harm potential / safety performance of consultation recommendations (NOHARM benchmark)
links.effect: RAG-based clinical AI tools outperformed generalist LLMs; no numeric effect given in the abstract
links.tradeoff: Even the RAG clinical AI tools carried potential for severe harm, with errors of omission accounting for more than 80% of severe errors across systems
links.quote: Harm potential was not uniform across systems, with clinical AI tools outperforming generalist LLMs, and multi-agent AI teaming further improving performance in generalist models.

links.comparator_used: Conventional resources (physicians working without AI assistance)
links.outcome: Physician performance on clinical consultation cases in a randomized study of 101 physicians
links.effect: AI assistance improved physician performance compared to conventional resources; no numeric effect given in the abstract
links.tradeoff: AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI-generated recommendations and still scored lower than many AI systems alone
links.quote: In a randomized study of 101 U.S.-licensed generalist physicians, AI assistance improved physician performance compared to conventional resources.

links.outcome: NOHARM clinical consultation safety/performance; potential for severe harm in recommendations
links.effect: Compared 4 widely used RAG clinical AI tools with 20 notable LLMs; clinical AI tools outperformed generalist LLMs; no between-arm numerical effect size reported in the supplied text.
links.quote: Harm potential was not uniform across systems, with clinical AI tools outperforming generalist LLMs, and multi-agent AI teaming further improving performance in generalist models.
